cases.command: mkdir -p /data/cpm && cd /data/cpm && printf x > a && chmod 750 a && cp a b && printf y > c && chmod 600 c && cp a c && mkdir -m 700 d && cp -r d e && umask 077 && cp a f && umask 022 && chmod 4755 a && cp a g && stat -c '%a %n' b c e f g
cases.note: Without -p, a file or directory cp makes takes the source's permission bits under the umask, setuid dropped, and a file that stood there keeps its own (debian:stable-slim).
